messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Incident detected — rapid region health flapping between us-east <-> us-west <-> eu. Symptom: routing fallback churn + elevated 5xxs for generation endpoints. See dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/INC-4156
anya: acked. paging devon and ops-oncall. setting P1.
devon: on it, grabbing logs. any recent policy changes?
ops-oncall: got the page, moving to #oncall-handoff. I'll keep pager duty open.
samira: noticed spikes in `model_variant` mismatch errors in eu last 10m — looks like a canary variant rolled out ~00:12 UTC.
devon: confirming — deployment id `canary-eu-4c9` started at ~00:11. healthcheck timeouts from the new variant: longer cold-starts + occasional OOM in local shard. That triggers health probes failing, which causes traffic to fallback to us-west, then us-west probes trip and fallback to us-east, creating a loop.
luis: adding telemetry: logs show repeated 504s from us-west -> kv-cache misses as it tries warmup. snippet: ```
[00:13:02] eu-node-12 healthcheck failed: 504 gateway timeout (startup)
[00:13:04] routing: eu -> us-west fallback
[00:13:05] us-west probe: probe fail (latency spike)
[00:13:07] routing: us-west -> us-east fallback
[00:13:08] us-east probe: ok -> routes back to eu (loop)```
anya: copy. impact? which customers hit 5xx/latency?
devon: quick query shows ~12 tenants saw 5xx for gen endpoints, error rate peaked ~18% for eu-origin traffic, global p95 latency for text-generation up from 210ms -> 1.8s. No data exfiltration.
samira: root cause likely twofold: 1) canary variant has heavier memory/initialization profile, 2) fallback policy is aggressive with immediate failover and mirrored health probes — no debounce.
ops-oncall: mitigation plan: (1) pause canary rollout in eu (rollback to stable variant), (2) temporarily set routing fallback delay and increase probe debounce, (3) pin critical tenants to `stable` in eu to reduce churn.
devon: executing rollback now: `redwoodctl deploy rollback --region eu --deployment canary-eu-4c9 --to stable-eu-2026-03-10`
console-bot: deploy rollback started for canary-eu-4c9 (initiated by devon). CI/CD job: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/9821
ops-oncall: while rollback in progress, applying routing soft-fail: ```
# reduce aggressive fallback, add 30s debounce
redwoodctl routing update --policy global-fallback --set fallback_debounce=30s --set prefer_local=true
```
anya: also temporarily disable cross-region mirrored probes for eu -> us-west to stop the immediate oscillation.
luis: applied probe config override: `probe.timeout=8s, probe.retries=3, probe.debounce=30s` for eu endpoints.
devon: rollback completed. canary removed, stable variant restored on eu nodes. health checks recovering.
pagerbot: Incident update: rollback succeeded; healthcheck fail count for eu decreased 90% in last 5m.
samira: monitoring shows routing churn dropped to baseline, error rate back to ~0.5%. verifying KV cache warmup and memory footprint on restored variant.
ops-oncall: customer comms: drafting message for affected tenants. proposed note: "Transient generation errors and elevated latency due to a canary variant rollout causing health probe flapping; rollback completed and services stabilized. We're following up with postmortem."
anya: agreed. send to the 12 affected accounts, cc account-success. Samira please add a link to logs and remediation steps.
samira: sending notifications now.
devon: post-incident actions I want: 1) block aggressive canary rollout if avg init latency > 500ms, 2) add automated `fallback_debounce` guard when enabling cross-region mirrors, 3) create telemetry alert for variant mem spike.
ops-oncall: assigning follow-ups: devon -> rollback circuit guard, samira -> canary perf gate, luis -> probe config defaults. I'll own the incident writeup.
anya: thumbs: :thumbsup: Good job. final status: mitigated, P1 resolved. We'll keep page open for 30m monitoring window.
pagerbot: Monitoring autopruned: all regions stable. Closing page in 25m if no regressions.
devon: leaving one note — review routing policy that allowed immediate back-and-forth: current fallback order = [local, nearest, least-cost], but health checks were symmetric. Recommend temporary change: prefer local with sticky session for 2 min after failover.
ops-oncall: noted. adding to postmortem.
console-bot: postmortem draft created: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-4156-postmortem (owner: ops-oncall).
anya: thanks team — good triage + quick rollback. final update to channel in 30m. :white_check_mark:
